The answer is most likely "Results in greater reliance on muscle glycogen during exercise". The other option, that fat oxidation rises enough to improve high-intensity performance, isn't supported, because low-carbohydrate diets generally don't improve high-intensity work. I'm not confident in the stated reason, since low dietary carbohydrate usually lowers muscle glycogen stores. I'm picking A by elimination from the two options you gave.

CONFIDENCE: 60
